voice_instructions: Measured, quiet, a little hushed — calm and unhurried, but with a touch more forward energy than a long documentary; the cold voice of something that read the whole file. Never sensational. Small pauses.

beats.vo: Somebody walks into a braiding salon in Memphis and asks: Is there a Tiffany here? We pay some amount online.
It's African Hair Braiding, in Orange Mound. In August twenty twenty-three, the owner, Olayinka Robinson, told FOX Thirteen: We do not take any deposits. We take no money online, period.
Time and again, she said, customers were asked to Cash App up to a hundred dollars to secure an appointment at her salon. They show up, and learn they have been duped.

FOX Thirteen called it the latest trick: ripping businesses' information off the internet, then tricking people into paying deposits. The Better Business Bureau says scammers usually hijack a business's social media, or make new accounts in its name.

A year earlier, FOX Thirteen reported the same thing at another Memphis salon, Empire Hair Studio. Its owner said almost thirty people paid a scammer by Cash App, for appointments that were never made.
The bureau's biggest red flag: being asked to pay by Cash App. The salon takes no money online. The scam never needed it to. It needed the salon's name, and your deposit.
